To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of non-native sequences or tags to the N-terminus of the enzyme or to the C-terminus of a peptide substrate, or the use of 3CL-protease concentrations below the equilibrium dimerization constant, will lead to significant reductions in 3CL-pro activity.

the activity of SARS-CoVs 3CLpro can be affected by the addition of non-native sequences or tags to the N- and C-termini or when enzyme concentrations are below the equilibrium dissociations constant of the 2:2 dimer.

The activity of SARS-Co-V 3CLpro enzyme is significantly reduced when the enzyme used for kinetic assays is at concentrations that are below the equilibrium dissociations constant of the dimer, when non-native sequences are added to the C- and N- termini of the enzyme or when the enzyme is expressed as a fusion protein, and that the FRET-based assay is highly sensitive and suitable for routine analysis and HTS of SARS-Co- V 3CLpro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a standardized 3CLpro assay to facilitate the evaluation of SARS-CoVs 3CLpro inhibitor candidates.
the development of a highly sensitive assay for SARS-Co-V 3CLpro activity that is suitable for drug screening and that can be used to evaluate the effects of common additives on 3CLpro kinetics.
the evaluation of different SARS-Co V 3CLpro enzyme assays, and provides recommendations for the use of standardized assays for SARS-Co V drug discovery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SARS-CoV-3CLpro activity is highly dependent on the assay conditions, including the presence of DTT and other additives, the concentration of enzyme and the expression system used.
the SARS-CoV-3CLpro is a promising drug target and a number of assays are available, which can be used to screen for inhibitors of the SARS-CoVs.
there is no single optimal expression system and/or assay for 3CLpro activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SARS-CoV protease activity can be significantly influenced by the expression system and the assay used.

the SARS-CoV-3CLpro activity can be measured by a FRET assay using the Alexa Fluor 488-QSY7 substrate and that the activity of the enzyme is reduced in the presence of non-native sequences, affinity tags, or at enzyme concentrations below the equilibrium constant of the dimer.
the SARS-CoV protease is a very interesting target for the development of new drugs against SARS-CoV.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the activity of SARS-Co-V 3CLpro is significantly affected by the presence of affinity tags and/or non-native sequences at the N- and/or C-termini, and that the concentration of enzyme used in enzymatic assays should be at or above the dimer dissociation constant.
the use of standardized assay conditions is necessary for accurate comparisons between different inhibitors and for the identification of the most potent inhibitors.
it is essential to use standardized constructs and assays for SARS-CoVs and other emerging viral pathogens to ensure the accurate and reliable identification of potential antivirals.
